text:
joan: Quick question — who is the *owner* of an API key when a service is used across multiple projects/orgs? thinking about a long-term model where ownership is explicit (person/team) vs implicit (project that created it).
ryan: I'd vote for service-principal/team ownership, not the project. projects come and go, teams persist.
maya: Agree. UI needs a transfer flow though. hard if key sits in 10 configs.
kevin: Audit + rotation implications are biggest pain. if ownership transfers we need a changelog entry and automated rotation window.
joan: Good point. Also wondering about delegating rotation: owners vs ops. who can rotate org-level keys?
ryan: Ideally only owner + security admins. But allow ops-bot to rotate under a controlled workflow (ticket, 2 approvals).
sec-bot: Related RFC: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/auth-key-lifecycle (TL;DR: prefer scoped keys, but fallback allowed).
maya: For migration, could we introduce explicit owner metadata on keys and a compatibility flag? e.g.
```
api_key: 1234...
owner: team/ingest-pipeline
compat: project-created-fallback=true
```
ryan: That seems low-risk. System reads owner first, falls back to project if owner missing and flags it as legacy.
kevin: Ops needs an automated sweep that finds keys without owners and inserts a placeholder owner and alerts teams. we can add TTL for those placeholders.
joan: How about cross-org use? some infra keys are intentionally shared across orgs (billing hooks, infra-alerting). who owns those?
maya: Make those "org-ambassador" owners — a single team mapped to cross-org infra. explicit and documented.
ryan: +1. Also add RBAC check: only owner/team or group-members can revoke/transfer.
kevin: We should add an audit webhook so security tooling can pick up owner changes. ops-bot can post to #audit.
ops-bot: will add a Jira template: AUTH-KEY-TRANSFER and a webhook hook if you want to test the flow. :robot_face:
joan: Migration plan sketch: 1) surface unknown-owner keys 2) auto-assign placeholders 3) notify owning teams 4) expose transfer UI + audit log 5) enforce owner-based RBAC after grace period. sound reasonable?
ryan: yep. also add an emergency rotate API usable by security admins with a forced TTL/rollback window.
maya: UI detail: make transfer a two-step confirm with current owner notified automatically. reduce accidental handoffs.
kevin: I'll draft the rotation/rollback runbook and add it to the RFC follow-up.
joan: Thanks all. I'll open a tiny RFC follow-up with the migration checklist and include sample DB patch + UI mock. will ping for review in ~24h. :thumbsup:
